patient._comment: 'patient' contains the three sections that may be exposed in the detailed patient display: presentation, answer, and clinical.

presentation._comment: The immutable patient evidence package available for triage. Panel context controls whether other sections are locked or available.
presentation.quote: I can't catch my breath, especially lying down — I've been sleeping upright in my recliner. My ankles are all puffed up and I've gained a few pounds just this week.
presentation.triageNote: 76-year-old female with progressive shortness of breath, now sleeping upright because she cannot breathe comfortably lying down. She reports recent weight gain and has bilateral ankle edema, bibasal crackles, and distended neck veins.

answer._comment: The authoritative game answer. Explicit ESI, destination, and destination rationale are answer-bearing content; the player's assignment remains session state.
answer.destinationReason: ESI 3 is appropriate because a stable but symptomatic fluid-overload presentation is expected to need multiple cardiopulmonary resources.

clinical._comment: Display-ready clinical interpretation derived from patient.presentation. It preserves clinical meaning but must not explicitly name or identify the correct ESI level or destination; it does not participate in scoring.
clinical.summary: This older adult has progressive dyspnea, orthopnea, weight gain, ankle edema, jugular venous distention, crackles, and mild hypoxemia.
clinical.acuityReason: She is not in severe respiratory distress, but the evidence of pulmonary and systemic congestion requires monitored evaluation and treatment.
expectedResources: Laboratory testing including cardiac and renal markers
keyFindings: Bibasal crackles and distended neck veins
teachingPoints: Orthopnea, edema, crackles, and weight gain together support a congestive pattern.
Worsening oxygenation, fatigue, hypotension, or inability to speak would increase urgency.

possibleClinicalOutcome.disposition: Cardiopulmonary testing and IV diuresis would likely be followed by monitored observation or admission, depending on oxygenation and treatment response.

aiImageGeneration._comment: 'aiImageGeneration' is info for AI to generate the image of the patient. Most images were done with openAI gpt-image-1 using an API, not the app, in July 2026. Look for some python scripts that are used to create these images. Be sure that the anchor-image is available and is provided to the AI - otherwise the images will not be consistent.
aiImageGeneration.pose: leaning forward on the chair, working to breathe
aiImageGeneration.prompt: Softly-shaded painterly cartoon illustration in a semi-realistic Pixar/Disney style: smooth gradient shading, soft natural lighting, gentle rounded volumes, fine delicate outlines (NOT thick flat cartoon outlines), warm detailed rendering, natural realistic proportions, single character, 3/4 front view, centered, square 1:1. Match the exact painterly style, brushwork, shading, line weight, lighting, and palette of the attached reference image. Subject: a black 76-year-old woman, seated on a blue padded clinic chair. Pose: leaning forward with hands on her knees, visibly working to breathe. Expression: tired and short of breath. Clearly visible: leaning forward breathing hard, with noticeably swollen ankles. No text, no logos.
